steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Features: A good speech is memorable, persuasive, and connects emotionally with the audience. It uses rhetorical devices to create impact and is designed to be heard, not just read. | : Introduction (Opening): Hook: Start with a striking statement, question, or anecdote Establish your credibility and purpose Connect with your audience | : Main Body: Present 3-4 key points Use one paragraph per point Support with evidence and examples Include rhetorical devices throughout Address counter-arguments if needed | : Conclusion (Ending): Summarise your main message End with a powerful call to action Leave a lasting impression

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: What is the purpose of a "hook" in a speech opening? | Name three rhetorical devices commonly used in speeches. | Write an opening paragraph for a speech about the importance of voting.

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on Key Features, Examiner's Tip, Speech Writing Exam Strategy, and one past-paper question.
